blocks.text: A bearing housing passes every plus-minus dimension on the inspection sheet, yet the shaft binds when it is assembled: the bore is 0.1 mm out of square with the mounting face. Size tolerances alone cannot say that bore and face must be square.

blocks.markdown: **Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T)** adds symbols that control **form, orientation, location and runout**, not just size. This unit follows the ASME Y14.5 convention, in which the tolerance is written in a **feature control frame (FCF)**, a rectangular box read from left to right and attached to a feature or its dimension.

blocks.title: Feature control frame
blocks.text: A **feature control frame** has compartments, left to right: (1) the **geometric characteristic symbol** (flatness, position, etc.); (2) the **tolerance zone**: a diameter sign if the zone is cylindrical, the tolerance value, and optionally a material condition modifier; (3) the **datum references**, in order of precedence: primary, secondary, tertiary.

Where a feature is relative to datums
Wobble of a surface of revolution about an axis
blocks.caption: The four families of geometric tolerance

blocks.title: Reading a feature control frame
blocks.prompt: An FCF on a hole reads, left to right: position, a diameter sign and 0.25 mm, a material-condition modifier M (maximum material condition), then datums A, B and C. Interpret it.

steps.text: The characteristic is position, a location control.
The diameter sign means the tolerance zone is a cylinder of diameter 0.25 mm centred on the theoretically exact position. The hole axis must lie within it.
M means the 0.25 mm applies when the hole is at its maximum material condition (smallest hole).
A, B, C: datum A is primary, B secondary, C tertiary, in order of precedence. The position is measured from the datum reference frame they establish.

blocks.answer: The hole axis must lie within a 0.25 mm diameter cylinder located from datum frame A | B | C, with M applying a bonus as size departs from MMC.

blocks.markdown: **Datum reference frame (DRF) and six degrees of freedom.** An unconstrained part has six degrees of freedom: three translations and three rotations. Three mutually perpendicular datum planes locate it. The **primary datum** (A) contacts the part at three points and removes 3 degrees (one translation along the datum normal and two rotations); the **secondary datum** (B) contacts at two points and removes 2 degrees (one translation, one rotation); the **tertiary datum** (C) contacts at one point and removes the last translation.

blocks.caption: Degrees of freedom removed by primary, secondary and tertiary datums respectively

blocks.title: Counting the datums
blocks.prompt: A rectangular plate rests on a large face (datum A), its long edge is pushed against two stops (datum B) and its short edge touches one stop (datum C). Count the DOF removed at each step and the DOF left after A and B only.

steps.text: Datum A contact at three points: 3 DOF removed (1 translation, 2 rotations).
Datum B contact at two points: 2 DOF removed (1 translation, 1 rotation).
Datum C contact at one point: 1 DOF removed (the remaining translation).
After A and B only, DOF left.

blocks.answer: After A and B one translation remains, removed by datum C. All 6 are fixed by A, B, C.

blocks.markdown: **Form tolerances** (flatness, straightness, circularity, cylindricity) govern the shape of one feature alone and take no datum. **Orientation** controls angle to a datum. **Location** controls where a feature sits relative to the DRF. **Runout** controls the variation of a surface of revolution measured while the part rotates about a datum axis: circular runout is checked at each cross-section, total runout over the whole surface.

blocks.title: Why order matters
blocks.text: The order of datum letters is the order of precedence: A then B is not the same as B then A, since the part is located first against A. Reading the order right is as important as the number.

items: Read the zone: diameter sign? value? modifier?
Read the datums in order: primary, secondary, tertiary.
Identify the family: form, orientation, location or runout.

points: A feature control frame holds a symbol, a tolerance zone with optional modifier, and ordered datum references.
A datum reference frame removes 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 degrees of freedom.
Form tolerances take no datum; orientation, location and runout do.

questions.stem: In a feature control frame reading 'angularity 0.1 A B', what does the order of the datum letters show?

options.text: The order of precedence: A is primary, B is secondary

questions.correctOptionText: The order of precedence: A is primary, B is secondary
questions.explanation: The part is located first against A, then B. Swapping them would define a different measurement set-up.

questions.stem: To which family does perpendicularity belong?
questions.explanation: Perpendicularity controls an angle (90 degrees) relative to a datum, so it is an orientation tolerance. Form tolerances take no datum, whereas orientation does.

questions.stem: A long shaft is located by datum axis A, which removes 4 degrees of freedom (two translations and two rotations perpendicular to the axis), and by an end shoulder face B, which removes the axial translation. How many degrees of freedom remain?
questions.explanation: Six minus 4 minus 1 leaves 1: the rotation about the shaft axis. This is why a keyway position needs a further datum or a stated angular reference.

questions.stem: A machined plate is checked with an indicator on a set-up already parallel to the measuring plane. The highest reading on the surface is 25.043 mm and the lowest is 24.998 mm. Calculate the flatness error (the zone width) in mm.
questions.explanation: The zone is the gap between two parallel planes that contain every point, so it is high minus low: 25.043 - 24.998 = 0.045 mm. A 0.05 mm flatness tolerance would be met.

questions.stem: An FCF reads 'position, diameter 0.2, datums A B'. What does the diameter sign mean?

options.text: The part must have a 0.2 mm hole
The tolerance zone is a cylinder 0.2 mm in diameter

questions.correctOptionText: The tolerance zone is a cylinder 0.2 mm in diameter
questions.explanation: A diameter sign before the value defines a cylindrical zone, here 0.2 mm across. It is not a size.

questions.stem: Which characteristic can NOT have a datum reference in its feature control frame?
questions.explanation: Cylindricity is a form control of one feature on its own, so it takes no datum. The others relate a feature to a datum.

questions.stem: A pattern of holes is toleranced for position relative to datum A only, where A is a large flat face. Which freedoms of the part remain uncontrolled?

options.text: Two in-plane translations and the rotation about the face normal
Two rotations about axes in the plane

questions.correctOptionText: Two in-plane translations and the rotation about the face normal
questions.explanation: Datum A removes the normal translation and the two tilts (3 DOF). The two in-plane translations and the spin about the normal still need B and C.

questions.stem: Interpret the feature control frame 'perpendicularity, 0.05, datum A' on a bore, stating the characteristic, family, zone and what is measured.
markingGuide: Zone: 0.05 mm wide, relative to datum A (a plane)
Bore axis (or surface) must lie within the zone perpendicular to A
questions.explanation: Marks for naming the family and describing the zone relative to the datum. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: Explain how a datum reference frame A, B, C removes the six degrees of freedom of a block, and why the order of precedence matters.
markingGuide: C: 1 point removes the last translation
Order sets which datum the part is located on first
questions.explanation: The marking guide gives credit for the 3-2-1 distribution and for the precedence argument. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: Circular runout and total runout both reference a datum axis.
questions.explanation: Runout is measured while the part rotates about a datum axis, so a datum is always needed. Circular runout checks one cross-section at a time and total runout checks the whole surface.
